title: Introduce contextual span weighting and token-cost conductor for observability
author: Jordan Kim
release_notes: Adds phase-aware span weighting, a token-cost conductor service, new dashboard panels, and an observability runbook entry.
description: Motivation: Long-tail latency and cost spikes often correlate with specific invocation phases and prompt shapes which are under-sampled by uniform trace capture. This PR implements a lightweight contextual span weighting algorithm to bias sampling toward spans with high phase-contribution and a coordinating token-cost conductor service that ties sampler budgets, token-cost estimates, and alert thresholds into a single runtime control plane. The result is higher-fidelity telemetry for the parts of the invocation lifecycle that drive cost and latency without increasing overall sampling volume. Design and changes: 1) span_weighting module implements a per-invocation phase scorer that consumes phased timing buckets and prompt-shape hashes to produce a dynamic weight for each span. 2) token_cost_conductor service exposes a gRPC control endpoint and REST read-only surface to allocate per-route sampling budgets, reconcile token-cost estimates with billing data, and emit sampling directives to downstream collectors. 3) telemetry samplers (prefetch and fallback samplers) were updated to honor span weights and conductor directives. 4) dashboards: new "Conductor Cost Rhythm" and "Phase Heatmap Detail" panels added to the observability space with linked drilldowns. 5) alerts: added adaptive alerting rule that scales alert thresholds by conductor-provided cost multipliers to reduce alert noise during known high-cost prompts. 6) docs and runbook: new runbook section describes how to tune conductor budgets, interpret phase-weighted traces, and rollback. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag observability.phase_weighting and conductor.enabled. Default rollout: internal canary in us-west for 48 hours, followed by staged rollout to all regions over one week. Observability validation: unit tests for span weighting and conductor reconciliation, integration test that simulates prompt-shape distribution and validates sampler directives, and a synthetic replay that shows 38% more high-impact spans sampled at equal budget. Backwards compatibility: collectors ignore conductor directives if the conductor is unreachable; sampling falls back to local defaults. Related work and tracking: links to linear tasks ENG-4217 and OBS-88 for tuning and alert adjustments.
